selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

experiences.name: Skiing at Jungfrau Ski Region
experiences.description: Experience world-class skiing across 213km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels. Families can enjoy dedicated beginner slopes in Grindelwald while advanced skiers tackle the challenging runs from Männlichen. Ski school lessons are available for children aged 3 and up, making it perfect for the whole family.

experiences.name: Glacier Paradise at Zermatt
experiences.description: Take the highest cable car in the Alps to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m and ski on year-round glacier snow. Families can explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, enjoy panoramic views of 14 four-thousand-metre peaks, and let kids experience the thrill of being on a real glacier. Includes a scenic gondola ride with stunning Matterhorn views.

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Experience
experiences.description: Join a hands-on culinary workshop in a traditional Alpine chalet where a local cheesemaker guides your family through the art of Swiss cheese production and authentic fondue preparation. Learn about centuries-old dairy traditions, taste regional cheeses, and sit down together to enjoy the fondue you made. A warm, memorable cultural experience perfect for all ages.

experiences.name: Winter Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run
experiences.description: Race down one of Switzerland's most thrilling natural toboggan runs stretching over 6km through snowy pine forests. Rent traditional wooden sleds and enjoy multiple runs as a family. The run is illuminated on select evenings for a magical night sledding experience. Hot chocolate and raclette are available at the base lodge, making it a perfect family afternoon adventure.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Journey
experiences.description: Board the iconic cogwheel train through two mountain tunnels to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Families can explore the Sphinx Observatory, walk through the Ice Palace, play in the snow plateau, and enjoy breathtaking views over the Aletsch Glacier — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A once-in-a-lifetime cultural and natural experience for all ages.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) train from Zurich Airport toward your Swiss Alps destination (approx. 1.5–2.5 hrs depending on exact location). Check into Aegean Bliss Resort, settle into your room, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit / on-board flight meal
meals.dinner: Grab a quick, affordable bite at Zurich Airport (Migros or Coop self-service restaurants, budget ~CHF 12–18 per person) before boarding the train.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or point-to-point SBB train ticket online in advance to save money. Validate your ticket before boarding. Luggage storage is available at Zurich Airport if needed. Keep warm layers accessible in your carry-on as Alpine temperatures at night can drop well below freezing in February.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then head to the nearest beginner-friendly ski slope for a morning orientation session. Rent ski equipment from a local rental shop near the resort (budget tip: look for 'Intersport' or 'Ski Service' rental shops which offer competitive daily rates of CHF 30–45 for a full set). Take a beginner or intermediate group ski lesson offered by local ski schools (approx. CHF 40–60 per person for a half-day group lesson).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the groomed pistes after your lesson. Explore the beginner and blue runs near the resort area. Take the gondola or chairlift up for scenic Alpine panoramic views even if you need a break from skiing. Visit the ski resort's free viewing platforms to enjoy the stunning snow-covered mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment and head back to the resort. Warm up with a cup of Swiss hot chocolate or Glühwein (mulled wine) at a cozy mountain hut or après-ski bar. Explore the nearby village on foot, browsing local shops and soaking in the charming Alpine atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort (included if offered, or grab bread, cheese, and yogurt from a local Coop or Migros supermarket for ~CHF 8–12 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch from the supermarket (sandwiches, fruit, hot thermos of soup) to eat on the slopes and save significantly vs. mountain restaurant prices. Budget ~CHF 10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local village restaurant offering Swiss staples like Rösti (potato dish) or cheese fondue. Look for set menus or 'Tagesmenü' (daily specials) which are significantly cheaper – budget ~CHF 20–30 per person. Try Restaurant Berghaus or similar local eateries.

day_by_day.notes: February in the Swiss Alps typically means excellent snow conditions. Book ski lessons in advance online to secure group rates. Families with children should inquire about dedicated kids' ski school programs, often available from age 3+. Helmets are strongly recommended and can be rented for ~CHF 5–8/day.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a snowshoeing adventure – a fantastic budget-friendly winter activity for the whole family. Rent snowshoes from local shops for approximately CHF 15–20 per person per day. Follow marked snowshoe trails through the snowy Alpine forests and meadows near the resort. Many trails are free to access and clearly signposted.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snowshoeing, visit a local toboggan (sledding) run. Many Swiss resorts have dedicated toboggan runs that are free or very low cost (CHF 5–10 for sled rental). This is a hugely popular and thrilling family activity. Alternatively, explore a nearby frozen lake or winter walking path for a peaceful afternoon stroll with spectacular mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the resort village's ice skating rink if available (entry typically CHF 8–15 per person including skate rental). Ice skating is a wonderful family evening activity. Afterward, head back to the hotel for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast from supermarket supplies – Swiss müsli, yogurt, fresh bread with butter and jam. Budget ~CHF 8 per person.
meals.lunch: Warm up at a mountain hut (Bergrestaurant) with a bowl of hearty Älplermagronen (Alpine mac and cheese) or Gulaschsuppe (goulash soup) – one of the most affordable hot mountain meals at ~CHF 14–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hotel room if kitchen facilities are available (pasta, supermarket sauces, salad) to save money. Budget ~CHF 8–12 per person. Alternatively, visit a local Coop or Migros deli section for ready-made meals.

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe trails are typically well-marked and suitable for all fitness levels including children. Always check trail conditions and weather forecasts before heading out. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers, insulating mid-layers, and a waterproof outer shell. Sunscreen is essential even in winter due to UV reflection off snow.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the ski slopes for a second day of skiing with improved confidence from Day 2. This time, challenge yourself with intermediate blue or red runs. Families can split up with children attending ski school while adults explore more challenging terrain. Purchase a half-day lift pass to save money if you plan to ski only in the morning (typically CHF 30–40 vs CHF 55–70 for a full day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic cable car or gondola to a high-altitude viewpoint (many included in lift pass). Enjoy the breathtaking 360-degree Alpine panorama. Visit a traditional Alpine dairy farm or cheese-making facility in the valley for a free or low-cost educational and cultural experience. Many farms welcome visitors in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Participate in a free or low-cost guided night snowshoe walk if offered by the resort or local tourism office. These torch-lit evening walks through snowy forests are magical and memorable for families. Check with the local tourist information office (Tourismusbüro) for free events and activities.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or supermarket self-catered option. Budget ~CHF 8–12 per person.
meals.lunch: On-slope picnic or affordable mountain hut lunch. Try Käseschnitten (toasted cheese bread) – a delicious and filling budget option at ~CHF 12–16.
meals.dinner: Enjoy a traditional Swiss cheese fondue evening at a local restaurant. Many places offer fondue sets for sharing which can be economical for families – budget ~CHF 22–28 per person. Look for restaurants away from the main tourist strip for better prices.

day_by_day.notes: Check the resort's website or local tourist office for any free family events, torchlit descents, or fireworks displays that often take place mid-week in February during ski season. Ask about family ski passes which often offer significant discounts for children under 9 who may ski free with a paying adult.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget-friendly regional train or PostBus to a nearby Alpine village or town for a day of cultural exploration and sightseeing. Visit the local church, town square, and traditional Alpine architecture. Many Swiss villages have free outdoor museums or heritage trails explaining local history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local winter market or artisan shops in the village. Browse handmade Swiss crafts, local cheeses, and chocolates. Visit a free or low-cost local museum (many Swiss regional museums charge CHF 5–10 entry). If near Grindelwald, Zermatt, or Interlaken area, enjoy the stunning views of iconic peaks like the Eiger, Matterhorn, or Jungfrau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by train or PostBus. Enjoy a relaxed evening walk through the illuminated village. Stop at a local bakery for affordable Swiss pastries (Gipfeli, Nusstorte) as an evening treat.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread rolls and coffee from a local bakery (Bäckerei) in the village – a very Swiss experience! Budget ~CHF 6–10 per person.
meals.lunch: Visit a local Migros or Coop restaurant in the nearby town – these supermarket cafeterias offer excellent value hot meals for CHF 10–15 per person and are very popular with locals.
meals.dinner: Back at the resort, try a local Pizzeria or casual restaurant for affordable dinner. Swiss pizzerias often offer excellent value with pizzas from CHF 16–22. Share a pizza between younger children to save costs.

day_by_day.notes: Switzerland's public transport system is excellent and punctual. Use the SBB app to plan routes and purchase tickets. The Swiss Travel Pass covers trains, buses, and some cable cars – calculate if it offers savings based on your travel plans. PostBus (PostAuto) routes reach many small Alpine villages not served by train.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a full day of winter sports with a focus on family fun. Head to the ski resort early to beat weekend crowds (Saturdays can be busier). Try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) as a budget-friendly alternative to downhill – trail passes are much cheaper (CHF 5–15) and equipment rental is lower. Many resorts have beautifully groomed cross-country tracks through scenic valleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Build snow sculptures or have a snowball fight in a designated open area near the resort. Visit the resort's terrain park if available for older children/teens to try snowboard jumps and features (with appropriate supervision and safety gear). Alternatively, enjoy a horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snow-covered landscape – a magical and memorable family experience (approx. CHF 20–40 per person for a short ride).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your last full active day with a special family dinner. Splurge slightly on a nice but still affordable Swiss restaurant for Raclette – melted cheese scraped over potatoes, pickles, and cold meats. A wonderful, interactive dining experience for families. Budget ~CHF 25–35 per person for this special evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or self-catered. Stock up on supermarket snacks and drinks for the day to minimize on-mountain food costs. Budget ~CHF 8–12 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack a hearty thermos of homemade soup and sandwiches from the hotel/supermarket for an on-slope picnic. Budget ~CHF 8–12 per person.
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss Raclette dinner at a local restaurant. Look for Raclette sets or all-you-can-eat options which offer better value. Budget ~CHF 25–35 per person for this special last-night splurge.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically the changeover day at many Swiss resorts so slopes and villages may be busier. Start activities early to avoid queues at lifts. Check if the resort offers any special Saturday evening events such as torchlit ski descents by the ski instructors – these are often free to watch and spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast and take a last morning walk through the resort village to soak in the Alpine atmosphere. Visit any local spots you may have missed during the week – a panoramic viewpoint, a historic chapel, or a scenic bridge. Take plenty of photos and purchase any last-minute affordable Swiss souvenirs (local cheese, chocolate bars from Coop/Migros are great value gifts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange transport to the train station. Take the scenic Swiss Federal Railways train back toward Zurich Airport, enjoying the stunning Alpine scenery one last time through the train windows. The train journey itself is a highlight of any Swiss trip.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Browse the duty-free shops for last-minute Swiss chocolate and souvenirs. Enjoy a final Swiss meal at the airport before departing.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a special treat at a local café – enjoy a Swiss Zopf (braided bread) with butter and honey, a Sunday morning tradition in Switzerland. Budget ~CHF 10–15 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack leftovers or grab affordable snacks from a Coop or Migros at the train station for the journey. Budget ~CHF 8–12 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich – Coop Restaurant or Marché offer good value options for CHF 15–22 per person. Alternatively, bring snacks for the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for travel to the airport – Swiss trains are reliable but it is wise to have a buffer, especially with luggage and children. Zurich Airport has excellent facilities including a dedicated family zone. Confirm your flight details and check-in requirements the evening before. Return any rented equipment (ski gear, snowshoes) the day before to avoid rushing on departure day.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Swiss Alps. Check-in and settle into your Beachfront accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort at approximately 23:30–00:00 after transfer. Light welcome snack at the hotel bar or room service. Review ski rental and activity options available at the resort concierge. Rest and recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or airport snack before departure
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night room service or hotel bar snack upon arrival — budget CHF 20–35 per person for a light bite

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer before arrival to avoid delays at night. Confirm ski rental reservations for Day 2 with the hotel concierge upon check-in. Pack warm layers in your carry-on as temperatures in the Swiss Alps in February can drop to -10°C or below at night.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then head to the resort ski school for a family orientation session and equipment rental fitting. Begin your alpine adventure with a half-day of Skiing at the Jungfrau Ski Region — 213km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels make this perfect for families. Beginners can take a 2-hour group ski lesson while more experienced skiers explore the blue and red runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau pistes after lunch. Take the Lauberhorn or Männlichen gondola for panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. Younger or less experienced family members can enjoy the dedicated beginner slopes and ski kindergarten areas. Take a mid-afternoon hot chocolate break at one of the mountain-top huts.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment or store at the resort locker. Warm up with a soak in the hotel's wellness facilities if available. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local Alpine restaurant in the nearby village.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — typically included or CHF 20–30 per person
meals.lunch: Mountain hut lunch on the slopes — try Rösti (Swiss potato cake) or a hearty soup. Budget CHF 25–40 per person at a mid-mountain restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local village restaurant — try traditional Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce) or cheese fondue. Budget CHF 40–60 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book ski school lessons in advance, especially during peak February school holiday season. Lift passes for Jungfrau Ski Region cost approximately CHF 70–85 per adult per day and CHF 35–45 per child. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers, insulating mid-layers, and a waterproof ski jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the hotel, then embark on the iconic Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Journey. Board the cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen, passing through two mountain tunnels to reach Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps, and explore the Ice Palace carved directly into the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — visit the Sphinx Observatory, the Snow Fun Park for snowtubing and zip-lining on the glacier, and take in 360-degree panoramic views across the Alps into France, Germany, and Italy on a clear day. Allow 4–5 hours total at the summit before taking the return cogwheel train down to the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a family-friendly dinner in Grindelwald or Interlaken village. Browse the charming Alpine shops for Swiss chocolates and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — arrive early to make the first morning train departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant or self-service restaurant at Jungfraujoch — budget CHF 30–50 per person. Prices are higher at altitude but the experience is unique
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Grindelwald village — try Raclette (melted cheese over potatoes) or Alpine pasta dishes. Budget CHF 35–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly in February. Round-trip tickets cost approximately CHF 145–160 per adult and CHF 75–80 per child from Grindelwald. The journey takes about 2 hours each way. Acclimatize slowly at the summit — altitude sickness is possible at 3,454m. Bring sunscreen as UV radiation is intense at high altitude even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: A fun and active morning — head to the Winter Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run, one of Switzerland's most thrilling natural toboggan runs stretching over 6km through snowy Alpine forest. This is a fantastic family activity suitable for all ages. Rent toboggans at the top and race down the winding natural run with incredible mountain scenery on all sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tobogganing excitement, warm up with lunch, then join the Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Experience — a hands-on culinary workshop in a traditional Alpine chalet. A local cheesemaker guides your family through the art of Swiss cheese production and traditional fondue preparation. Learn about different Alpine cheese varieties including Gruyère, Emmental, and Appenzeller.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary labor — eat the fondue you made during the workshop as part of the experience. Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Optional: visit the hotel spa or wellness center for tired muscles after an active day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a mountain café near the toboggan run — try a warm Bratwurst with bread or Alpine soup. Budget CHF 20–30 per person
meals.dinner: The fondue making workshop typically includes tasting the prepared dishes. Supplement with a light dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby bistro — budget CHF 25–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch toboggan run is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the Jungfrau region — confirm exact location and travel time with the hotel concierge. Toboggan rental costs approximately CHF 10–15 per sled. The cheese and fondue workshop typically costs CHF 60–90 per adult and CHF 30–45 per child and lasts 2–3 hours. Book both activities in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Zermatt for the Glacier Paradise experience. Travel by train to Zermatt (car-free village) and take the highest cable car in the Alps to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m. Ski on year-round glacier snow with the iconic Matterhorn pyramid dominating the skyline. The glacier runs are wide, gentle, and perfect for family skiing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing the Zermatt glacier area — explore the Italian-Swiss border skiing at Cervinia if conditions allow. More adventurous family members can try the longer red runs descending from the glacier. Take a break at a mountain restaurant with unbeatable Matterhorn views. Begin descending back to Zermatt by 15:00–15:30 to explore the village.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the charming car-free village of Zermatt — browse the boutiques, visit the Alpine Museum, and admire the iconic Matterhorn at golden hour. Enjoy dinner in Zermatt before taking the train back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start recommended for the Zermatt day trip
meals.lunch: Lunch at a glacier restaurant on Klein Matterhorn — try Swiss mountain specialties like Älplermagronen (Alpine macaroni with cheese and applesauce). Budget CHF 35–55 per person
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zermatt village — try a traditional Swiss restaurant serving Walliser Teller (local charcuterie platter) or beef fondue. Budget CHF 45–65 per person

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is approximately 2–2.5 hours from the Grindelwald/Interlaken area by train — depart early (07:00–08:00) to maximize time on the glacier. The Glacier Paradise cable car costs approximately CHF 100–120 per adult round trip. Zermatt is a car-free village — take the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn train from Täsch. Bring extra sun protection as glacier altitude is extreme.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — sleep in and enjoy a full hotel breakfast. Use the morning for a gentle snowshoe walk or cross-country skiing on beginner-friendly tracks near the resort — a wonderful low-intensity alternative to downhill skiing, perfect for the whole family. Alternatively, visit the resort's indoor pool or spa for a wellness morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Jungfrau Ski Region for a final afternoon of skiing. Focus on runs you enjoyed most during Day 2, or challenge yourselves with slightly more advanced pistes. Take a scenic gondola ride for panoramic Alps photography. Stop at a mountain hut for a traditional Swiss Glühwein (mulled wine for adults) and hot chocolate for children.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell-to-the-slopes dinner at a highly-rated local Alpine restaurant. Celebrate the week's adventures with a traditional multi-course Swiss meal. After dinner, enjoy a family board game night or stargazing from the resort terrace — February skies in the Alps are spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the slopes or at a mountain hut — pick up fresh bread, local cheese, and cold meats from a village bakery or deli. Budget CHF 15–25 per person
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a top-rated local restaurant — try a 3-course meal with Alpine appetizer, main course of veal or lake fish, and Swiss chocolate dessert. Budget CHF 55–80 per person

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically the busiest day on the slopes due to weekend visitors — head to the lifts early (09:00) to beat the queues. If the family is tired from the week's activities, this is an ideal day to scale back and enjoy the resort's amenities. Check ski equipment return procedures with the rental shop.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Pack luggage and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take one last walk through the Alpine village to soak in the mountain scenery. Visit a local bakery for fresh Swiss croissants and a coffee. Pick up last-minute Swiss souvenirs — Swiss chocolate (Lindt, Toblerone), local cheese, or a Swiss Army knife are classic gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final light activity — a scenic train ride through the Bernese Oberland, a visit to the Trümmelbach Falls (frozen waterfalls in winter), or a leisurely café stop in Interlaken. Begin transfer to the airport with ample time for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, glacier adventures, Swiss culinary experiences, and family memories in one of the world's most beautiful mountain destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab-and-go from a village bakery — budget CHF 10–20 per person
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Interlaken or at the airport — try a Swiss sandwich (Sandwich mit Käse) or a warm pretzel with mustard. Budget CHF 20–30 per person
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant dinner or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours for the transfer from the Swiss Alps to Zurich Airport (ZRH) or Geneva Airport (GVA) depending on your departure airport. Swiss trains are punctual and reliable — consider taking the scenic train rather than a taxi for a memorable final journey. Confirm hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. Declare any food items (cheese, meat products) at customs when returning home.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.dinner: In-suite late-night dining: Gourmet Swiss welcome platter arranged by the resort — featuring Gruyère, Raclette, cured Alpine meats, fresh-baked bread, and warm Glühwein. Pre-arranged with the concierge prior to arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked through the resort concierge. Request early suite preparation so everything is warm and ready upon late arrival. Pack ski gear or arrange ski rental reservations for the following morning before departing your home country.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start after the late arrival. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, visit the resort's premium ski concierge to arrange custom-fitted ski equipment, private ski instructor bookings, and lift passes for the week ahead. Take a relaxed orientation stroll around the resort and nearby village to acclimatize to the altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your Alpine ski adventure with an introductory private ski lesson at the Jungfrau Ski Region — 213km of immaculately groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels. Hire a certified private PADI/ISIA ski guide for the family to assess skill levels and explore beginner-to-intermediate runs. The vast terrain ensures every family member has a tailored, exhilarating experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a rejuvenating session at the luxury spa — heated indoor pool, sauna, and après-ski massage treatments. Dress for a refined dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grand Alpine Breakfast Buffet at the resort's main restaurant — freshly baked croissants, Swiss bircher muesli, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, farm eggs cooked to order, fresh-pressed juices, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountaintop lunch at a premium ski-in/ski-out restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — try Rösti with mountain herbs, Alpine soup, and hot chocolate with whipped cream.
meals.dinner: Signature fine-dining dinner at the resort's flagship restaurant — a 4-course Alpine-inspired tasting menu featuring local venison, truffle risotto, and a Swiss chocolate fondant dessert, paired with curated Swiss wine selections.

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructors at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Ensure all family members have appropriate layered ski clothing, helmets, and UV-protection goggles. Altitude acclimatization is important — drink plenty of water throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at the Jungfrau Ski Region with your private ski guide. Morning session focused on advancing ski technique across intermediate and advanced blue and red runs. The family can split into skill-appropriate groups, each with a dedicated instructor. Enjoy the panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks as you carve through pristine powder.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the afternoon on the Jungfrau slopes. For non-skiing family members or those seeking a break, arrange a private horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snow-covered Alpine meadows — a magical, luxurious alternative. Reconnect as a family at the mid-mountain terrace for hot drinks and panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski experience at an exclusive Alpine lounge — live acoustic music, artisan cocktails, and Swiss craft beers. Then return to the resort for a private in-suite fondue dinner experience, with a personal chef preparing traditional Swiss cheese fondue tableside in your suite.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast in-suite — eggs Benedict with smoked Alpine trout, fresh fruit platter, warm pastries, and French press coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium ski chalet restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — Älplermagronen (Swiss Alpine macaroni), braised beef cheeks, and warm apple strudel with vanilla cream.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite fondue dinner prepared by a personal resort chef — traditional Swiss cheese fondue (Gruyère and Emmental blend), Bündnerfleisch, gherkins, and pearl onions, paired with a crisp Swiss Chasselas white wine.

day_by_day.notes: The horse-drawn sleigh ride should be booked the day before through the concierge. Ensure ski passes are valid for the full Jungfrau region to maximize terrain access. In-suite dining requires advance notice of at least 4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Iconic day trip: Board the legendary Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' cogwheel train — a UNESCO World Heritage railway experience. Depart early from Grindelwald or Wengen station. The train winds through two dramatic mountain tunnels to reach Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, walk on the glacier, and marvel at the breathtaking Aletsch Glacier views. A truly unforgettable family memory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — visit the Sphinx Observatory, try the snow fun park (sledding and snow tubing available at the summit), and browse the Top of Europe exhibitions. Descend back by early afternoon and enjoy some time in the charming village of Grindelwald — browse luxury Alpine boutiques and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private family movie night arranged by the butler in your suite — popcorn, Swiss hot chocolate, and a curated selection of films. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's casual fine-dining bistro.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — continental spread with Swiss cold cuts, cheeses, yogurt parfait, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Restaurant at 3,454m — a truly unique dining experience above the clouds. Enjoy warm Alpine soups, Swiss sausages, and hot beverages while gazing at the eternal snow.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's Alpine Bistro — a relaxed yet refined setting. Try the Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (Zurich-style veal in cream sauce with Rösti), followed by a decadent Swiss chocolate tart.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly, especially in peak season. Dress in extra warm layers — temperatures at 3,454m can be -15°C or colder with wind chill. Sunrise departures offer the clearest views and fewest crowds. Altitude sensitivity may affect some family members — carry water and light snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Paradise at Zermatt — a full-day premium excursion. Take a private luxury transfer to Zermatt (car-free village). Board the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car — the highest in the Alps — ascending to Klein Matterhorn at 3,883m. Ski on the year-round glacier with stunning views of the iconic Matterhorn peak. A private mountain guide leads the family on the glacier ski runs, suitable for intermediate and advanced skiers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue glacier skiing or explore the Zermatt ski area's legendary red and black runs with your private guide. For younger family members or beginners, arrange a private snowshoeing excursion across the glacier plateau — equally spectacular and accessible. Descend to Zermatt village in the afternoon to explore the charming pedestrian streets.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive dinner in Zermatt at one of the village's Michelin-starred or top-rated restaurants before the private transfer back to the resort. Zermatt's dining scene is world-class — an unmissable culinary highlight of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast at the resort before departure — bircher muesli, smoked meats, artisan breads, soft-boiled eggs, and freshly squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise summit restaurant — panoramic views of 14 countries on a clear day. Enjoy hot Alpine dishes, fondue, and warming beverages at nearly 4,000m altitude.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium Zermatt restaurant — recommended: Restaurant Zum See (a legendary Alpine hut restaurant) or Chez Vrony on the slopes. Seasonal Alpine cuisine, exceptional Swiss wine list, and an intimate romantic atmosphere surrounded by mountain scenery.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — only electric taxis and horse-drawn carriages operate within the village. Private transfer drops you at the village entrance. Book Zermatt restaurant reservations weeks in advance as they are extremely popular. Glacier skiing requires appropriate high-altitude equipment — confirm rental arrangements in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Experience — an immersive, hands-on culinary workshop in a traditional Alpine chalet. A local master cheesemaker guides the family through the art of Swiss cheese making and the history of fondue culture. Learn the secrets of Gruyère and Raclette production, and craft your own cheese blend to take home as a luxury souvenir. A wonderfully interactive and educational experience for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Winter Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run — one of Switzerland's most thrilling natural toboggan runs, stretching over 6km through pristine snow-covered forest and mountain terrain. Race the family down this legendary run for pure exhilaration and laughter. Multiple runs can be enjoyed throughout the afternoon. Private hot chocolate and warm snacks await at the finish line.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury spa and wellness evening at the resort — couples' or family spa packages, heated outdoor infinity pool overlooking the snowy Alps, aromatherapy steam rooms, and signature Alpine massages using local herbs and mountain spring water. Cap the evening with a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort's main restaurant — à la carte options including fluffy Swiss pancakes with mountain berry compote, eggs any style, smoked salmon, and specialty teas.
meals.lunch: Traditional Swiss lunch included as part of the cheese and fondue workshop — taste your own handcrafted cheeses alongside fresh Alpine bread, cured meats, and local wines in the authentic chalet setting.
meals.dinner: Celebratory family dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — a 5-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairing. Highlights include foie gras with Alpine honey, pan-seared lake perch, aged Swiss beef tenderloin, and a showstopping Swiss chocolate soufflé.

day_by_day.notes: The cheese-making workshop should be booked through the concierge at least 3 days in advance as group sizes are limited. Toboggan runs can be busy on weekends — arrive early afternoon for shorter queues. Spa treatments should be booked in advance to secure preferred time slots. Children's spa menus are typically available for younger family members.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — one last private ski session on your favorite runs at the Jungfrau Ski Region. Savor the mountain air, the views, and the joy of the slopes with the family. Return equipment to the ski concierge and collect any personalized mementos arranged by the resort (custom ski day photo books, engraved Swiss chocolates, or personalized cheese wheels from the workshop).
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely checkout experience — no rush. Enjoy a long farewell lunch at the resort. Spend the remaining afternoon exploring the resort's amenities, taking final photos of the Alpine scenery, or visiting the village for last-minute luxury souvenir shopping — Swiss watches, premium chocolates, Alpine spirits, and artisan crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer departs from the resort to Zurich Airport or onward destination. Enjoy a chilled Champagne send-off from the resort staff. En route, reflect on an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps — world-class skiing, glacier adventures, culinary masterclasses, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — the full Alpine spread. Freshly baked goods, artisan cheeses, smoked fish, seasonal fruit, yogurt with honey, and premium specialty coffees and teas.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the resort's terrace restaurant (weather permitting, dine outdoors with Alpine panorama views) — light yet indulgent: truffle pasta, Alpine salad with mountain herbs, and a glass of Swiss sparkling wine.
meals.dinner: In-transit or upon arrival at next destination. If departing late, arrange a gourmet picnic hamper from the resort for the journey — artisan sandwiches, Swiss chocolates, local cheeses, fruit, and a bottle of Swiss wine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange checkout and transfer timing carefully to allow adequate time for airport procedures. Request the resort to prepare a luxury farewell hamper for the journey. Ensure all ski rental equipment is returned before checkout. Confirm private transfer booking the evening before departure. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers ski-related activities for future trips.
